evals.name: grants-reviewer-dashboard
evals.prompt: I'm building an internal admin tool for our college's research-grants office. Faculty submit grant proposals and our staff reviewers approve or send them back. Design the reviewer's landing page — what should they see the moment they log in? Give me the layout and enough detail that a developer could build it.
evals.expected_output: A work-queue-first landing (not a link hub): linkable stat tiles, a queue table of pending proposals with inline review actions, concrete 8px-grid spacing and semantic color tokens, an accessibility pass (contrast/focus/keyboard), empty/loading states, and Tailwind/implementation guidance. Should default to the CCC house style.

evals.name: secondary-appointment-form-flow
evals.prompt: Design the form a faculty member fills out to request a secondary appointment at another department. It collects their name, home department, the target department, appointment type, and a CV upload, then gets routed by email to approvers. Walk me through the UX — the flow and what each screen looks like.
evals.expected_output: A user flow with the happy path plus error/empty branches, a wireframe/layout, form design following the prefill/labeling doctrine (labels above fields, required marking, CV-upload handling, specific inline errors, one primary action), designed loading/empty/error/success states, a mobile/responsive note, and an accessibility pass. Concrete tokens and sizes throughout.

evals.name: status-badge-component-spec
evals.prompt: Across our apps we keep reinventing status badges and they all look slightly different — approved, pending, under review, changes requested, rejected. Give me one proper status-badge component we can standardize on, with the color tokens, so it's consistent everywhere.
evals.expected_output: A component spec in a reusable format (variants for each status, all relevant states, radius/type/padding tokens), a status color system with a text tone + paired tint background per status, documented WCAG-AA contrast, a note that status is not conveyed by color alone (icon/label), and cva/Tailwind implementation guidance. Should map onto the CCC house tokens.
